page.read_only: Connecting providers and saving keys is up to an administrator; here you can see their status.
page.issues_description: Turn open findings into issues for your team, with no duplicates across scans.

ai.title: AI assistance
ai.description: An explanation of each finding and a proposed patch, using your own OpenAI or Anthropic key. It will be optional and isn't available yet: today AI takes no part in any scan, and there's no key to save.

plan.consent: Consent on every run before anything is sent to the provider
plan.budget: A per-run budget and secret redaction
plan.no_code: Source code is never sent without that consent

ai.saved_key: a key saved earlier (····{{last4}}) is kept but not used
ai.plan_intro: When it arrives, it will come with:

jira.tagline: Create issues from findings, in the project each repository belongs to
jira.label_note: Each issue carries the label appsec-<fingerprint>: exporting the same finding again links the existing issue instead of creating a duplicate.
jira.remove_help: Pitangus stops creating and commenting on issues. Existing issues stay in Jira, and destinations and rules are kept for when you connect again.
jira.validate_note: The account is checked against Jira before saving. The token stays on the server and never comes back to the browser. Then choose where issues go.

destinations.title: Destinations
destinations.help: A Jira project and issue type, and what Pitangus puts in each of its fields.
destinations.empty: No destinations yet. Add one to choose the project and issue type your issues go to.
destinations.legacy: Set up in an earlier version: edit and save it to choose what goes in each field.
destinations.remove_help: Issues already created stay in Jira. No rule uses this destination.
destinations.editor_help: Pick the project and issue type from Jira, then check what goes in each field. Pitangus suggests a mapping you can keep as is.
destinations.name: Name
destinations.no_projects: No project matches, or the account can't see it.
destinations.locale: Language of its issues and comments
destinations.on_fixed_move: Verified fix: comments, adds {{label}} and moves the issue to {{status}}
destinations.on_fixed_move_only: Verified fix: comments and moves the issue to {{status}}

mapping.title: Fields
mapping.help: Required fields are marked. Fields left empty take Jira's default, if there is one.
mapping.caption: What Pitangus puts in each field of the issue
mapping.truncated: This issue type has more fields than Pitangus lists; only the first ones appear here.
mapping.unsupported_help: Users, cascading selects, links and similar fields: Pitangus leaves them empty.
mapping.unsupported_reason: Pitangus can't fill this kind of field. Give it a default value in Jira or choose another issue type.
mapping.required: Jira requires this field: choose what goes in it
mapping.required_unsupported: Jira requires this field and Pitangus can't fill it
mapping.incomplete: Complete the value, or choose Leave empty

rules.title: Rules
rules.help: Each repository follows the first rule that matches it, from the top. The last rule covers the rest.
rules.matches_rest: Every repository no rule above matches
rules.no_destination: No destination: findings of these repositories don't go to Jira
rules.rerun_backfill: Create issues for open findings again
rules.saved_backfill_one: Rule {{name}} saved: {{count, number}} issue queued for open findings.
rules.saved_backfill_other: Rule {{name}} saved: {{count, number}} issues queued for open findings.
rules.remove_help: Its repositories fall to the next rule that matches them. Issues already created stay in Jira.
rules.editor_help: Pick repositories, name patterns or both. The first rule that matches a repository decides where its issues go.
rules.default_help: This rule covers every repository no other rule matches. Turn it off to send only what other rules match.
rules.name: Name
rules.patterns_help: One per line. * matches any text: org/payments-* covers every repository whose name starts that way.
rules.mode_auto_help: Pitangus creates them for new findings from full scans, imports and new advisories. Never for PR reviews.
rules.backfill: Also create issues for findings already open
rules.backfill_help: Paced to respect Jira's limits. What already has an issue is linked, not duplicated.
rules.rerun_title: Create issues for open findings of {{name}}?

preview.needed: Check what this rule would create before saving.
preview.outdated: The rule changed: check again what it would create.
preview.result_one: It would create {{issues}} issue now · open findings: {{findings}} · repositories: {{assets}} · already linked: {{linked}}
preview.result_other: It would create {{issues}} issues now · open findings: {{findings}} · repositories: {{assets}} · already linked: {{linked}}
preview.nothing: Nothing to create now: no open finding without an issue matches (already linked: {{linked}}).
preview.truncated: Only the first {{max}} findings are queued; the rest go in the next run.
preview.sample: The most severe one will read like this in Jira:

backfill.running_one: Creating issues for open findings: {{count, number}} queued
backfill.running_other: Creating issues for open findings: {{count, number}} queued
backfill.truncated: limit reached: run it again for the rest
backfill.done: Finished creating issues for open findings on {{date}}

finding.no_rule: No rule sends this repository to Jira

export.intro: One issue per piece of work: advisories for the same package go together, with the version that fixes them all; code and secrets go one by one. Anything that already has an issue gets linked, not duplicated.
export.intro_target: They go to {{target}}. One issue per piece of work: advisories for the same package go together; code and secrets go one by one. Anything that already has an issue gets linked, not duplicated.
export.relinked_one: {{count, number}} had an issue that was deleted in Jira: created again
export.relinked_other: {{count, number}} had issues that were deleted in Jira: created again

queue.intro: More than {{max}} findings go through the queue: this window closes and Pitangus creates the issues in the background, a few seconds apart. Follow them from the Jira indicator at the top.
queue.progress_one: {{done}} of {{total, number}} issues · {{pending}} in the queue
queue.progress_other: {{done}} of {{total, number}} issues · {{pending}} in the queue

background.started_one: Creating {{count, number}} issue in Jira in the background
background.started_other: Creating {{count, number}} issues in Jira in the background
background.nothing_one: Nothing to create: {{count, number}} finding already had an issue
background.nothing_other: Nothing to create: {{count, number}} findings already had an issue
background.label: Jira {{done}}/{{total, number}} · issues being created in the background
background.label_done: Jira · issues created in the background
background.title: Jira issues in the background
background.help: Your large selections. They keep going if you close or reload the page.
background.forced: new issues even if already linked
background.none_routed: Nothing to queue: no rule sends these findings to Jira

force.title: Create new issues anyway
force.explain_one: Pitangus creates a new issue for this finding and links it instead of the current one. The current issue stays in Jira, untouched.
force.explain_other: Pitangus creates a new issue for each of these {{count, number}} findings and links it instead of the current one. The current issues stay in Jira, untouched.

on_fixed.title: When a scan verifies the fix
on_fixed.help: Pitangus always comments on the issue. It moves the issue only if you pick a status here: every team closes issues its own way.
on_fixed.label: Label to add
on_fixed.label_hint: Leave it empty for none. With a label, the fixed issues are one search away in Jira.
on_fixed.status_hint: Statuses of this issue type's workflow. If an issue can't move there from its current status, the comment says so.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: A message in Slack, Teams or a webhook when a scan (manual, batch or automatic) finds something new that matters, or when a batch finishes. Pull request reviews already notify on the pull request itself.

hint.slack: In Slack, open Apps, find Incoming Webhooks and click Add to Slack; pick the channel and copy the URL (https://hooks.slack.com/…).
hint.teams: In Teams, open the channel's … menu, choose Workflows and the "Post to a channel when a webhook request is received" template, then copy the URL.
hint.webhook: Any service that accepts a JSON POST. Every notification carries the X-Pitangus-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256 of the body).

notifications.saved: Channel "{{name}}" saved. Send a test to check it.
notifications.confirm_remove: To add it back you'll need the webhook URL again.
notifications.test_failed: The test to "{{name}}" failed: {{detail}}. Check the URL or create the webhook again.
notifications.secret_title: This webhook's signing secret: save it now, it won't be shown again.
notifications.secret_help: The receiver computes an HMAC-SHA256 of the body with this secret and compares it with the X-Pitangus-Signature header.
notifications.name: Name
notifications.url_note: The URL is stored encrypted and never comes back to the browser.
notifications.links_note: To have messages link to the finding, set PITANGUS_PUBLIC_URL to the panel's address.

row.none_hint: Add Slack, Teams or a webhook.
